2) Dedicated tests explicitly tied to this story all pass: - Command run: npm test -- --verbose - Result: Test Suites: 35 passed, 35 total; Tests: 266 passed, 266 total. - File: tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts - Header: - @story docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md - @req REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC, REQ-ERROR-SUGGESTION, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-ERROR-LOCATION - Valid case ensures existing @story annotation produces no error. - Main test "reports specific message, data, and suggestions for function 'bar'": - Uses a synthetic Program + FunctionDeclaration("bar") and calls rule.create(context). - Asserts one report entry. - Asserts rule.meta.messages.missingStory is a non-empty string containing "{{name}}". - Asserts error.messageId === "missingStory". - Asserts error.data === { name: "bar", functionName: "bar" }. - Asserts error.suggest is an array with at least one element. - Asserts first suggestion.desc is "Add JSDoc @story annotation for function 'bar', e.g., /** @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md */" and has a defined fix function.
3) Rules implement the specified error message patterns and data wiring: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - meta.messages.missingStory: "Function '{{name}}' must have an explicit @story annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @story that points to the implementing story file (for example, docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md)." - hasSuggestions: true, fixable: "code". - JSDoc on rule references docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md and REQ-ERROR-MSG-* requirements. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?): - If hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node) is true, returns early (no false positives). - Computes functionName via extractName and uses it for both "name" and "functionName" in data. - Chooses an identifier node (id/key) as the reported node for accurate location. - Calls context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingStory", data: { name, functionName: name }, fix: createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget), suggest: [{ desc: `Add JSDoc @story annotation for function '${name}', e.g., /** @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md */`, fix: createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget) }] }). - reportMethod does the same for methods, also including functionName in data and anchoring on the method name.

6) Format and validation error conventions are implemented: - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - meta.messages.invalidStoryFormat / invalidReqFormat / invalidImplementsFormat: each: "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}.". - Commented as implementing REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-ERROR-CONSISTENCY for Story 007.0. - Implementation uses buildStoryErrorMessage / buildReqErrorMessage to fill "details" with specific explanations (missing vs invalid, path vs ID). - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts - Many cases assert correct reporting for missing path/ID, invalid formats, multi-line annotations, custom patterns, and invalid config, all via these messageIds.
7) File and reference error patterns are implemented: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - meta.messages: - fileMissing: "Story file '{{path}}' not found" - invalidExtension: "Invalid story file extension for '{{path}}', expected '.story.md'" - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{path}}'" - fileAccessError: "Could not validate story file '{{path}}' due to a filesystem error: {{error}}. Data fields like functionName, path/storyPath, reqId allow formatter/IDE integration. - Error-handling helpers (e.g., try/catch around hasStoryAnnotation and reportMissing in require-story-helpers, fs error handling in valid-story-reference) prevent crashes when context is incomplete or IO fails and instead produce clear diagnostics (fileAccessError, etc.). - Dedicated edge-case tests for require-story IO and helpers (tests/rules/require-story-io.edgecases.test.ts, tests/rules/require-story-helpers-edgecases.test.ts) confirm that unusual sourceCode shapes and missing APIs are handled gracefully.
10) Documentation of conventions: - docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md itself describes the exact message patterns implemented (functionName placeholders, missingAnnotation with {{missing}}, Invalid annotation format: {{details}}., filePath/reqId conventions, and severity rules). - Rule files have JSDoc tying specific meta.messages entries back to this story and its REQ-ERROR-* IDs, ensuring in-code documentation matches the spec.
traceability.notes:
The story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING defines cross-cutting requirements for clear, actionable, and consistent error messages across all traceability rules. Implementation of these requirements is visible in the meta.messages definitions and reporting logic of the six core rules, and is validated by multiple test suites.
The dedicated tests in tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts confirm that require-story-annotation produces a specific, template-based message with the correct {{name}} placeholder, includes both name and functionName in the data payload, and provides ESLint suggestions with a concrete example fix. Similar patterns are used for require-req-annotation via annotation-checker helpers.
Branch-level errors use the shared "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}." pattern, format rules use "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}.", and file/reference rules use messages that include the problematic path and/or reqId. Severity mappings (errors for missing/invalid traceability, warnings for non-breaking format issues) are enforced and tested through the plugin configs.
All relevant tests pass, edge cases (invalid config, filesystem errors, missing comments or sourceCode APIs) are handled without crashes, and documentation in the story and JSDoc comments aligns with the implemented behavior. Therefore, all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are satisfied, and the story is fully implemented.
